description: Make a running timer announce its time every every_seconds (1 to 60, default 5) as a timer.tick event tagged with topic. Listeners connect to GET /sse or to GET /mcp on an initialized session, and may filter with ?events=timer.tick&topic=demo. The first tick is sent at once. The pushing ends when the timer is stopped or its countdown ends; every_seconds 0 stops it early and leaves the timer running. Pass for_seconds to end it after that long: on a stopwatch (a clock heartbeat) the timer is stopped then, so start_timer without seconds plus push_timer with for_seconds=120 sends the time every few seconds for two minutes. If events are off, push_timer switches on the timer events itself (timer.started, timer.tick, timer.finished, timer.stopped) so a timer demo needs no admin credential; an administrator can turn that off with update_settings with events.autoTimer=false. Other events (log lines, tickets, settings) still need update_settings (events). This is not how you read a timer; read it with run_query schema=timers.

every_seconds.description: Seconds between ticks, 1 to 60. Default 5. 0 stops the pushing and leaves the timer running.

for_seconds.description: Report for this many seconds, 1 to 3600, then end. A stopwatch (a clock heartbeat) is stopped then; a countdown just stops reporting. Leave out to report until the timer ends.

timer_id.description: A running timer from start_timer. Format: TMR-1. Do not invent an id.

topic.description: Tag for the events, so a listener can filter with ?topic=. Defaults to the timer's label.

name: push_timer
